paragraph: The S&P 500 -- the index that tracks 500 large U.S. companies -- closed at 7,827, about 7.0% above its long-term trend line. Above that line is what people mean by a bull market: prices rising over months, not just days. Today's news flow leans careful -- willing, but watching the exits. The loudest themes in the headlines: Middle East Tension, Russia Ukraine, Trump Tariff Negative. Put trend and headlines together and the combined read is 'risk-on': conditions favour patience with a plan over reacting to any single headline.
what_it_means: A bull trend describes the recent past. It is not a forecast, and it has never once meant 'prices only go up from here.'
Trouble in oil-producing regions moves energy prices first, and everything that runs on fuel after that -- one reason it leads market news even if you never think about oil.
This digest is market vocabulary in plain English, for learning only -- never a tip on what to buy or sell.
